\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Gaussian Bobkov}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.GaussianBobkov
\section{Overview}
Normalized Boolean-block derivatives approximate the Euclidean coefficient length of a smooth derivative family. Passing to the Gaussian limit proves Bobkov bounds for probability-valued functions with bounded Lipschitz derivatives.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Length under coordinate perturbations]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.sqrt_sq_add_sum_sq_le_add_error}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For a finite set $I$, a real scalar $P$, and vectors $d,g\in\mathbb R^I$, $\sqrt{P^2+\sum_i d_i^2}\le\sqrt{P^2+\sum_i g_i^2}+\sqrt{\sum_i(d_i-g_i)^2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Length bound for a repeated gradient]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.sqrt_sq_add_array_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.sqrt_sq_add_sum_sq_le_add_error}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$, $m>0$, $P\in\mathbb R$, $d\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$, $g\in\mathbb R^n$, and $e\ge0$. If $|d_{ij}-g_i/\sqrt m|\le e$ for every $i,j$, then $\sqrt{P^2+\sum_{i,j}d_{ij}^2}\le\sqrt{P^2+\sum_i g_i^2}+\sqrt{nm}\,e$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded continuous Bobkov integrand]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_boundedContinuous_bobkov_integrand}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuousOn_closedGaussianProfile,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_closedGaussianProfile}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,1]$ be continuous, and let $D(z)$ be a continuous family of real linear functionals on $\mathbb R^n$ with $\|D(z)\|\le M$ for all $z$, for some real $M$. Then $z\mapsto\sqrt{\overline I(f(z))^2+\sum_i(D(z)e_i)^2}$ is a bounded continuous function.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Vanishing accumulated block error]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_block_gradient_error}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every $n\ge0$ and $C\in\mathbb R$, $\sqrt{n(m+1)}\,2C/(m+1)\to0$ as $m\to\infty$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bobkov bound on normalized Boolean blocks]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkov_normalizedBoolBlocks_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_normalizedBoolBlocks_half_difference_sub_derivative_le,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkov_inequality_array,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.sqrt_sq_add_array_sq_le,BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,1]$ be differentiable with derivative family $D(z)$, globally $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm for the maximum norm, where $C\ge0$. Write $|D(z)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(D(z)e_i)^2}$. For independent uniform bits $X_{ij}$, put $S_r(X)_i=r^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^r(-1)^{X_{ij}}$. For every $m>0$, $\overline I(\mathbb E f(S_m(X)))\le\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f(S_m(X)))^2+|D(S_m(X))|_2^2}+\sqrt{nm}\,2C/m$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Smooth Gaussian Bobkov inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_bobkov_smooth}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkov_normalizedBoolBlocks_le,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_closedGaussianProfile,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_boundedContinuous_bobkov_integrand,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_block_gradient_error,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolBlocks,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,1]$ be differentiable with derivative family $D(z)$, globally $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm for the maximum norm, where $C\ge0$. Write $|D(z)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(D(z)e_i)^2}$. If also $\|D(z)\|\le M$ for every $z$, for some $M\in\mathbb R$, then $\overline I(\int f\,d\gamma_n)\le\int\sqrt{\overline I(f(z))^2+|D(z)|_2^2}\,d\gamma_n(z)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of bounded gradient length]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianGradient_of_bounded}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_zero,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_boundedContinuous_bobkov_integrand,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Let $D(z)$ be a continuous family of real linear functionals on $\mathbb R^n$ and let $M\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\|D(z)\|\le M$ for all $z$. Then $z\mapsto\sqrt{\sum_i(D(z)e_i)^2}$ is $\gamma_n$-integrable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Separated smooth Gaussian Bobkov bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_bobkov_smooth_le_sum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_nonneg,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_bobkov_smooth,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_closedGaussianProfile_comp,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianGradient_of_bounded,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,1]$ be differentiable with derivative family $D(z)$, globally $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm for the maximum norm, where $C\ge0$. Write $|D(z)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(D(z)e_i)^2}$. If also $\|D(z)\|\le M$ for every $z$, for some $M\in\mathbb R$, then $\overline I(\int f\,d\gamma_n)\le\int\overline I(f)\,d\gamma_n+\int|D(z)|_2\,d\gamma_n(z)$.
\end{lemma}
